title: A/P Summary sorts lower-case accented and joined letters as plain letters
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Six vendors have open bills on today's date: {Vendor-A}, {Vendor-B}, {Vendor-C}, {Vendor-D}, {Vendor-E} and {Vendor-F}. {Vendor-B} has "æ" and {Vendor-E} has "ß" in its name.
    For example: {Vendor-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-04 Ackley, {Vendor-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-04 æble, {Vendor-C} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-04 Afton, {Vendor-D} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-04 Strand, {Vendor-E} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-04 Straße and {Vendor-F} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-04 Strasser.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Finance > A/P Summary is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Without clicking any column header, find the six vendors in the list.
  2. Read their order from top to bottom.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: all six vendors are listed.
  • Step 2: they read {Vendor-A}, {Vendor-B}, {Vendor-C}, {Vendor-D}, {Vendor-E}, {Vendor-F}. With the example names, "æble" sorts as "aeble" (between "Ackley" and "Afton") and "Straße" sorts as "Strasse" (after "Strand", before "Strasser").

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order)

  • S1-R1: “A/R Summary opens with customers in name order, A to Z; A/P Summary opens with vendors in name order, A to Z.”
  • S1-R3: “Accented letters sort with their base letter: "Émile's" sorts among the E names (é è ê ë sort as e, á à â ä ã å as a, ç as c, ñ as n, ö ó ò ô õ ø as o, ü ú ù û as u, í ì î ï as i, ý ÿ as y, ß as ss, æ as ae, œ as oe, in both cases).”
